Subject: Aurora11b - transient server-side timeouts & committed mitigations

Hi Elena / Skyline ops team,

Quick note to surface an elevated rate of server-side timeouts and 5xx errors affecting calls routed to the aurora11b generation family between ~07:38 and 08:03 PST this morning. Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate (sync), /v1/chat/stream (streaming). We saw a peak 5xx-rate of ~4.6% across your traffic slice and latency tail increase from p95 220ms -> 1.8s.

What we did immediately:
- Scoped traffic to aurora11b-v2-rw (variant) and throttled long-token requests over 4k tokens.
- Enabled emergency routing to aurora11b-slim (compatible fallback) for new requests to reduce error surface.
- Evicted 3 nodes identified with persistent OOM traces and force-drained pods for reallocation.

We attached a small log bundle that contains sampled traces and host-level metrics from the affected cluster. We are continuing to monitor and will share an interim update within 4 hours.

Requested from you: if you have a correlation id or internal ticket for the customer-observed incidents (Skyline ticket id helps), please share so we can link.

Apologies for the interruption — we know these errors are disruptive. We will credit impacted token usage for the window if the spike materially affected production traffic.

Attachments: aurora11b-spike-logs-20281209.zip (log bundle); mutual-action-plan_SKY-4123.pdf (MAP draft)

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Elena / Skyline ops,

Interim summary and actions taken (12:10 PST):

Root cause (interim): our telemetry indicates a regression in the kernel-selection heuristic introduced in the 12/08 runtime roll that misclassified high-token, multi-turn requests as short sequences. That path bypassed a hot-KV cache placement optimization and produced elevated memory pressure on a subset of hosts, which manifested as OOM-originating timeouts and 5xx responses.

Mitigations applied:
- Rolled back the kernel-selection heuristic to the previous stable version (12/08 07:56 GMT rollback).
- Evicted 3 affected hosts and rebalanced traffic away from the impacted zone.
- Increased autoscaler buffer (temporary +30% headroom) and temporarily lowered the circuit-breaker sensitivity for Skyline traffic to avoid aggressive drops while routing to aurora11b-slim.

Observed result: error rate on your traffic has dropped from peak 4.6% -> 0.3% over 20 minutes, and p95 latency is back to baseline ~240–260ms. We will continue to watch for regression over the next 48 hours.

Next steps and asks from Skyline:
- Confirm whether you still see truncated replies in the UI (we expect context was preserved for replayed requests routed to slim variant, but please validate).
- If you can share a few example correlation IDs from SKY-4123, we will include them in the RCA bundle.

I've attached the sampled trace logs and a draft mutual action plan outlining rollback, verification, and postmortem owners. Our postmortem doc will be available in the Drive link provided once the internal review is complete.

Attachments: aurora11b-spike-logs-20281209.zip; mutual-action-plan_SKY-4123.pdf

Thanks for your patience — we will follow up with a full RCA that includes a code-level patch and degradation test coverage within 72 hours.

Best,
Monica Patel

Subject: Aurora11b incident: RCA link and closure items

Elena / Skyline ops — final note and closure items.

We completed the internal postmortem and the code patch for the kernel-selection heuristic has been backported and test-covered. The postmortem highlights:
- Trigger: kernel-selection heuristic misrouted long-sequence requests to a memory-inefficient execution path after a runtime commit during 12/08 deploy.
- Immediate impact: increased memory pressure on 3 hosts -> OOM-related connection resets -> elevated 5xx/timeouts for requests routed to those hosts.
- Fix: rollback + targeted patch to avoid heuristic misclassification; additional unit tests and a small synthetic degrader test added to CI to prevent regressions for long-sequence routing.

What we provided to Skyline:
- Full log bundle & traces (attached earlier)
- Postmortem doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroraPostmortem
- Credit proposal: one-time credit covering the impacted window (07:38–08:05 PST), ready pending approval from finance.

Open action items:
- Redwood to finalize DocuSign for the credit approval (DOCUSIGN-REQ-8921).
- Redwood infra to run a focused blast test in staging for aurora11b long-sequence traffic patterns; results due 2028-12-11 EOD.

If Skyline is satisfied, we will mark SKY-4123 as resolved and close the loop. Thanks again for partnering through the incident — feel free to ping me directly if you'd like a postmortem walk-through this week.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
